title: Supported dumbbell reverse lunge
instructions: Stand tall beside a sturdy support, holding one dumbbell in the opposite hand.
Step one foot backwards and lower the back knee towards the floor only as far as feels controlled.
Keep most of your pressure through the front foot and push through it to return to standing.
Complete the reps on one side, then swap legs and hands.
form_cues: Keep the front knee tracking in line with the toes.
Use the support for balance rather than pulling yourself back up.
regressions: Perform the movement without a dumbbell.
Use a supported split squat with a shorter range.
progressions: Increase the comfortable range of motion before adding more weight.

title: Bench hip thrust
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the edge of a stable bench and feet flat around hip-width apart.
Brace gently and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Pause briefly at the top while squeezing your glutes without over-arching your lower back.
Lower your hips under control and repeat.
form_cues: Keep your chin gently tucked and ribs down at the top.
The bench must be stable and unable to slide before you start.
progressions: Place a padded dumbbell across the hips.
Pause for two seconds at the top of each rep.

title: Dumbbell biceps curl
instructions: Stand tall or sit upright holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms by your sides.
Keep your elbows close to your body and curl the weights towards your shoulders.
Pause briefly without letting your elbows drift forwards.
Lower the dumbbells slowly until your arms are long and repeat.
form_cues: Avoid swinging your body to move the weights.
Keep wrists neutral rather than bending them backwards.
regressions: Alternate one arm at a time.
progressions: Increase load gradually once all reps are controlled.

title: Seated dumbbell triceps extension
instructions: Sit tall on a sturdy chair or bench and hold one dumbbell securely with both hands above your head.
Keep your upper arms fairly still and bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head through a comfortable range.
Straighten your elbows to return the dumbbell overhead without forcing them hard straight.
Repeat slowly and finish the set before lowering the dumbbell safely.
form_cues: Keep ribs down instead of arching your lower back.
Stop if the overhead position causes sharp shoulder or elbow pain.
regressions: Use a resistance-band triceps press-down if overhead movement is uncomfortable.

title: Resistance-band lateral walk
instructions: Place a loop resistance band above your knees and stand with feet about hip-width apart.
Soften your knees slightly and keep your chest tall.
Step sideways under control, then bring the other foot in without letting the band go completely slack.
Complete the planned steps in one direction, then return the same number of steps.
form_cues: Keep knees tracking over the toes rather than collapsing inward.
Take controlled steps instead of bouncing or dragging the trailing foot.
regressions: Perform fewer steps with a smaller knee bend.
progressions: Place the band lower on the legs only when control is reliable.

title: Seated cable row
instructions: Set the cable row to a manageable weight, sit securely and take hold of the handle.
Sit tall with arms long and shoulders relaxed away from your ears.
Pull the handle towards your lower ribs while your elbows travel back beside your body.
Return the handle slowly until your arms are long again without rounding forwards excessively.
form_cues: Keep your torso mostly still instead of rocking backwards to move the weight.
Finish the pull by moving the elbows back, not by shrugging the shoulders.
progressions: Increase the weight gradually once all reps remain controlled.
Pause for one second with the handle near your ribs.

title: Treadmill purposeful walk
instructions: Start the treadmill at an easy walking pace and settle for two minutes.
Increase the pace or incline slightly until the effort feels purposeful but controlled.
Maintain the effort while walking naturally and using the rails only if needed for safety.
Reduce the speed for the final two minutes before stepping off once the belt has stopped.
form_cues: Choose a pace where you could still speak a short sentence.
Do not hold a steep incline if it changes your walking pattern or causes pain.
regressions: Walk more slowly with no incline.
progressions: Add two to five minutes before increasing intensity.
Increase incline slightly while keeping the same controlled pace.

title: Open-book thoracic rotation
instructions: Lie on your side with hips and knees comfortably bent and both arms reaching forwards together.
Keep your knees stacked as you slowly sweep the top arm open and rotate your upper body towards the floor behind you.
Pause where the stretch feels comfortable without forcing the shoulder down.
Return the top arm to the start, finish the reps and then change sides.
form_cues: Let the movement come from your upper back rather than forcing your lower back to twist.
Keep the motion smooth and pain-free.
regressions: Support the top arm on a pillow at the end of the movement.
progressions: Pause for two slow breaths in the open position.
Straighten the lower leg while keeping the top knee supported if comfortable.
